[Rocky Ledge.]

A broad, open ledge of white-grey opens up on a floor of stone too dense and uniform to allow for much vegetation.  A squat, oval structure with coal black accents dominates the center of the area.  Not far from it, a slouching pile of dull grey ash spreads out and down the gentle slope of the ledge.  Positioned higher than the tallest nearby trees to the east and north, the spot offers a magnificent vista.  Clear weather would allow views not only of a distant shimmering sea between peaks to the east, but a small protruding island as well.  The north sky is blocked by high, snow-capped mountains.  The air is cool, damp, and breezy at this height.  A small stream collects on the western edge near the trees, in a perfectly rectangular basin, before falling down into a deep vertical slit.  You notice a limestone kiln, and the body of a giant white-furred yeti.

[Above Rocky Ledge.]

A broad, open ledge of white-grey opens up below on a floor of stone too dense and uniform to allow for much vegetation.  A squat, oval structure with coal black accents dominates the center of the area.  Not far from it, a slouching pile of dull grey ash spreads out and down the gentle slope of the ledge.  Positioned higher than the tallest nearby trees to the east and north, the spot offers a magnificent vista.  Clear weather would allow views not only of a distant shimmering sea between peaks to the east, but a small protruding island as well.  The north sky is blocked by high, snow-capped mountains.  The air is cool, damp, and breezy at this height.  A small stream collects on the western edge near the trees, in a perfectly rectangular basin, before falling down into a deep vertical slit.

Obvious Exits: down, east, and south.

[Rocky Ledge.]

A broad, open ledge of white-grey opens up on a floor of stone too dense and uniform to allow for much vegetation.  A squat, oval structure with coal black accents dominates the center of the area.  Not far from it, a slouching pile of dull grey ash spreads out and down the gentle slope of the ledge.  Positioned higher than the tallest nearby trees to the east and north, the spot offers a magnificent vista.  Clear weather would allow views not only of a distant shimmering sea between peaks to the east, but a small protruding island as well.  The north sky is blocked by high, snow-capped mountains.  The air is cool, damp, and breezy at this height.  A small stream collects on the western edge near the trees, in a perfectly rectangular basin, before falling down into a deep vertical slit. [Narrow Crevice.]

The hard limestone surface has been polished by centuries of flowing water, leaving behind bowls, swirls, and gentle curves as it meandered along over time. [Narrow Crevice.]

The hard limestone surface has been polished by centuries of flowing water, leaving behind bowls, swirls, and gentle curves as it meandered along over time.  Some mosses and small tufts of grasses have taken hold, but for the most part the limestone walls remain bare and glossy.  The crevice is large enough for even the larger forest beings to move along it unseen from ground level, but the slick, irregular surfaces apparently discourage animal traffic, except for birds that swoop down from the trees in search of insects or a playful, refreshing splash-about in one of the cool, natural bowls.

[Rocky Ledge.]

A broad, open ledge of white-grey opens up on a floor of stone too dense and uniform to allow for much vegetation.  A squat, oval structure with coal black accents dominates the center of the area.  Not far from it, a slouching pile of dull grey ash spreads out and down the gentle slope of the ledge.  Positioned higher than the tallest nearby trees to the east and north, the spot offers a magnificent vista.  Clear weather would allow views not only of a distant shimmering sea between peaks to the east, but a small protruding island as well.  The north sky is blocked by high, snow-capped mountains.  The air is cool, damp, and breezy at this height.  A small stream collects on the western edge near the trees, in a perfectly rectangular basin, before falling down into a deep vertical slit.  You notice a limestone kiln.

Obvious Exits: east, and south.

Clouds the size of towering mountains continuously float across clear patches of blue sky like glaciers across icy waters.  Brief gaps in the clouds provide glimpses of the vast landscape below, as if looking through a portal into another world. A blurry haze rises up from the perimeter of the clouds, circling the area like a protective halo.

[Abandoned Limestone Quarry.]

Covered with moss and lichens, an irregular series of right-angled steps mark the locale of a modest quarry cut into the side of the mountain.  Huge iron links still dangle from the stone, remnants of some kind of crane system to deliver blocks to the road below.  Dark, stagnant water collects at the base of the quarry, while saplings struggle to find nourishment in long abandoned cracks and crevices.

Obvious Exits: northeast, and west.

[Narrow Crevice.]

The hard limestone surface has been polished by centuries of flowing water, leaving behind bowls, swirls, and gentle curves as it meandered along over time.  Some mosses and small tufts of grasses have taken hold, but for the most part the limestone walls remain bare and glossy.  The crevice is large enough for even the larger forest beings to move along it unseen from ground level, but the slick, irregular surfaces apparently discourage animal traffic, except for birds that swoop down from the trees in search of insects or a playful, refreshing splash-about in one of the cool, natural bowls.

se



[Tree Line.]

Small clumps of snow hide in the northern shadows despite the season.  Short, stubborn alpine grasses remain the only scenery against the many jagged, prominent rock outcroppings.  The wind is harsh, cold, and relentless.

Obvious Exits: northwest, and west. 

nw



[Steep Rocky Incline.]

White lines and ridges of snow no longer hide only within the deep shadows.  Snow accumulates anywhere the sun cannot continually reach, or the wind cannot readily sweep clean.  Only scattered rocks or the rare, stubborn bush provides such protection.  Not even a sapling tree can be found on this cold, wind-swept ridge leading to the very peak.

Obvious Exits: southeast. 

u



[Steep Rocky Incline.]

Snow accumulates on the side of the mountain.  No trees or visible boulders can be found this high up.  To the east, a mountainous island can be discerned within the sea, while far to the southwest, a robust city is barely recognized at first glance, snug against the sea.

Obvious Exits: southeast, and down. 

u



[High In The Sky, Crowns Summit.]

This appears to be one of the higher peaks of the region.  However, the view west to north is blocked by other peaks, seemingly formed in alternating rows.  To the east, a mountainous island can be discerned within the sea, while far to the southwest, a robust city is barely recognized at first glance, snug against the sea.

Also here: a giant white-furred yeti, and a giant white-furred yeti

w



[Rugged Alpine Meadow.]

The trees are thin as a high-altitude meadow takes over a bit of level area.  Game trails and droppings are scattered about.  Large swathes of long white-haired, cotton grass sway in the strong breezes, oftentimes shedding their floral snow.  Nearby branches continually ebb and flow, rustling in the wind.  Far below, the remains of a road and bridge can be discerned beyond the deliberate cuts and angles of a long-abandoned quarry.

Obvious Exits: southeast, and east. 

se



[Steep Rocky Incline.]

The trees are stunted and wind-swept, their branches sweeping generally to the east, while their twisted trunks lean west down the mountain side.  Great boulders and rock outcroppings compete with the struggling trees in height.  Grasses are prominent, clinging to the rocky soil despite the prevalent gusts of cold, harsh wind.

Obvious Exits: southwest, and northwest. 

sw



[Abandoned Limestone Quarry.]

Covered with moss and lichens, an irregular series of right-angled steps mark the locale of a modest quarry cut into the side of the mountain.  Huge iron links still dangle from the stone, remnants of some kind of crane system to deliver blocks to the road below.  Dark, stagnant water collects at the base of the quarry, while saplings struggle to find nourishment in long abandoned cracks and crevices.

Obvious Exits: northeast, and west. 

w



[Rocky Ledge.]

Providing a brief respite from the arduous climb both ascending and descending, this little ledge allows a spectacular view to the east, of both the nearby mountains and the distant sea that glimmers far beyond.  Chisel marks and regularly spaced hand holds demonstrate that this was once part of an intentionally constructed route up and down the steep cliff.

Obvious Exits: west, and east. 

w



[Rocky Ledge.]

A broad, open ledge of white-grey opens up on a floor of stone too dense and uniform to allow for much vegetation.  A squat, oval structure with coal black accents dominates the center of the area.  Not far from it, a slouching pile of dull grey ash spreads out and down the gentle slope of the ledge.  Positioned higher than the tallest nearby trees to the east and north, the spot offers a magnificent vista.  Clear weather would allow views not only of a distant shimmering sea between peaks to the east, but a small protruding island as well.  The north sky is blocked by high, snow-capped mountains.  The air is cool, damp, and breezy at this height.  A small stream collects on the western edge near the trees, in a perfectly rectangular basin, before falling down into a deep vertical slit.  You notice a limestone kiln.

Obvious Exits: east, and south.

[Steep Rocky Path.]

Hugging the base of a steep limestone rock face, the way is crowded with fallen, chalky rocks, as well as the occasional tree or bush that has taken root among them.  Dense foliage blocks any view of the mountain summit.  In the distance to the east, amidst gaps in the trees can be glimpsed a far shimmering ocean framed by two peaks.

Obvious Exits: south, and north.

[Narrow Streambed.]

A modest, yet fast-flowing stream comes out of a deep, limestone cut to the south; wide enough for single filed travelers to enter well below the ground level at either side.  Here however, due to a change in consistency of the stone, the stream spreads out and meanders around roots and boulders.  Pine trees sway in the winds above, but the air down here is relatively still and cool.

Obvious Exits: south, and north.

Pine boughs sway high above, their roots snaking down along the hard stone, searching out the water, and providing convenient hand holds to proceed along the otherwise smooth, wet, and slippery crevice.

[City of Pearl, Center.]

Granting an uninhibited view of the bustling shipping industry, a stone seawall bevels out behind a long crescent bench and creates a half-moon addition to the congested crossroads at the heart of the city.  The vast water of the bay expands beyond the southern stone wall.  Ships of all sizes pass by the seafront as they make their way in and out of the harbor to the south.  The streets head in many directions, as well as a tunnel to the northeast.  At the center of the intersection is an elegantly carved monument of a giant pearl atop a tall obelisk.  The base of the centerpiece rests at the bottom of a shallow fountain that has a burning spear pointing down into the water.  A small stone sundial has been carved on the rim of the fountain.  You notice a wooden directional signpost. 

Also here: Trystan the Human, Flynt the Sylph (flying), Seren the Avardi, Eabo the Goblin, Champion Blink the Avardi, Kaiah the Human, Wren the Human, a lavishly dressed merchant, Kaiya the Avardi, Kristauf the Human, Kody the Vukasin, a navy blue-robed constable, a lavishly dressed merchant, and Pyratherndar the Vukasin

Obvious Exits: southwest, southeast, northwest, northeast, there, west, east, and north.

[Narrow Crevice.]

The hard limestone surface has been polished by centuries of flowing water, leaving behind bowls, swirls, and gentle curves as it meandered along over time.  Some mosses and small tufts of grasses have taken hold, but for the most part the limestone walls remain bare and glossy.  The crevice is large enough for even the larger forest beings to move along it unseen from ground level, but the slick, irregular surfaces apparently discourage animal traffic, except for birds that swoop down from the trees in search of insects or a playful, refreshing splash-about in one of the cool, natural bowls.

Obvious Exits: west, and north.

[Narrow Crevice.]

Tumbling and swirling about at the bottom of the crevice, the stream continues its relentless work slowly cutting into the hard stone.  The top of the crevice is now high above the steep, slippery limestone walls.  Evidence of the stream's past indecision lie everywhere, leaving long-forgotten ledges, slots, and pot-holes that now serve as convenient hand holds as well as natural pots for bits of grass and even the doomed sapling tree or bush.

Obvious Exits: northwest, and east. 

nw



[Narrow Crevice.]

The crevice jogs sharply from the northwest and downstream to the southeast.  The constant splash of a hip-high waterfall at the turn can be heard throughout the area.  At the waterfall's base, a basin contains a relatively calm pool.  Ice clings to the deep, dark recess just behind the falls, regardless of season.  You notice an underground cavern.
nw

Obvious Exits: southeast. 

nw



[Underground Cavern.]

The aquatic cavern is spacious due to the years of cyclic ice melt that have stripped it of all but the remaining rocky walls and crumbling stone floor.  Above, water trickles down from a shaft in the ceiling.  Areas of the uneven floor rise above the waterline, atop which lies many large bones and other uneaten remains.  The dark, flowing water that comes underneath the walls escapes through a dim crevice to the southeast.  You notice some piles of bones, a narrow crevice, a splintered iron-banded oak chest, a large tooth-gouged oak chest, a half-eaten wyvern carcass, and a large mound of ore deposits.

Obvious Exits: none

[Narrow Crevice.]

The hard limestone surface has been polished by centuries of flowing water, leaving behind bowls, swirls, and gentle curves as it meandered along over time.  Some mosses and small tufts of grasses have taken hold, but for the most part the limestone walls remain bare and glossy.  The crevice is large enough for even the larger forest beings to move along it unseen from ground level, but the slick, irregular surfaces apparently discourage animal traffic, except for birds that swoop down from the trees in search of insects or a playful, refreshing splash-about in one of the cool, natural bowls.

[Narrow Crevice.]

Tumbling and swirling about at the bottom of the crevice, the stream continues its relentless work slowly cutting into the hard stone.  The top of the crevice is now high above the steep, slippery limestone walls.  Evidence of the stream's past indecision lie everywhere, leaving long-forgotten ledges, slots, and pot-holes that now serve as convenient hand holds as well as natural pots for bits of grass and even the doomed sapling tree or bush.

Obvious Exits: northwest, and east.

[Narrow Crevice.]

The hard limestone surface has been polished by centuries of flowing water, leaving behind bowls, swirls, and gentle curves as it meandered along over time.  Some mosses and small tufts of grasses have taken hold, but for the most part the limestone walls remain bare and glossy.  The crevice is large enough for even the larger forest beings to move along it unseen from ground level, but the slick, irregular surfaces apparently discourage animal traffic, except for birds that swoop down from the trees in search of insects or a playful, refreshing splash-about in one of the cool, natural bowls.

Obvious Exits: west, and north.

[Narrow Crevice.]

The hard limestone surface has been polished by centuries of flowing water, leaving behind bowls, swirls, and gentle curves as it meandered along over time.  Some mosses and small tufts of grasses have taken hold, but for the most part the limestone walls remain bare and glossy.  The crevice is large enough for even the larger forest beings to move along it unseen from ground level, but the slick, irregular surfaces apparently discourage animal traffic, except for birds that swoop down from the trees in search of insects or a playful, refreshing splash-about in one of the cool, natural bowls.

Obvious Exits: west, and north. 

w



[Narrow Crevice.]

[Rocky Ledge.]

A broad, open ledge of white-grey opens up on a floor of stone too dense and uniform to allow for much vegetation.  A squat, oval structure with coal black accents dominates the center of the area.  Not far from it, a slouching pile of dull grey ash spreads out and down the gentle slope of the ledge. [Rocky Ledge.]

A broad, open ledge of white-grey opens up on a floor of stone too dense and uniform to allow for much vegetation.  A squat, oval structure with coal black accents dominates the center of the area.  Not far from it, a slouching pile of dull grey ash spreads out and down the gentle slope of the ledge.  Positioned higher than the tallest nearby trees to the east and north, the spot offers a magnificent vista. The air is cool, damp, and breezy at this height.  A small stream collects on the western edge near the trees, in a perfectly rectangular basin, before falling down into a deep vertical slit. The air is cool, damp, and breezy at this height.  A small stream collects on the western edge near the trees, in a perfectly rectangular basin, before falling down into a deep vertical slit.  You notice a limestone kiln. 

Obvious Exits: east, and south. 

e



[Above Rocky Ledge.]

Providing a brief respite from the arduous climb both ascending and descending, the ledge below allows a spectacular view to the east, of both the nearby mountains and the distant sea that glimmers far beyond.  Chisel marks and regularly spaced hand holds demonstrate that this was once part of an intentionally constructed route up and down the steep cliff.
down

Obvious Exits: down, west, and east. 

e



[Above Abandoned Limestone Quarry.]

Covered with moss and lichens, an irregular series of right-angled steps mark the locale of a modest quarry cut into the side of the mountain below.  Huge iron links still dangle from the stone, remnants of some kind of crane system to deliver blocks to the road farther below.

Obvious Exits: northeast, down, and west. 

ne



[Above Steep Rocky Incline.]

The trees below are stunted and wind-swept, their branches sweeping generally to the east, while their twisted trunks lean west down the mountain side.  Great boulders and rock outcroppings compete with the struggling trees in height.  Grasses are prominent, clinging to the rocky soil despite the prevalent gusts of cold, harsh wind.

Obvious Exits: southwest, northwest, and down. 

nw



[Above Rugged Alpine Meadow.]

The trees are thin as a high-altitude meadow takes over a bit of level area.  Game trails are scattered about.  Large swathes of long white-haired, cotton grass sway in the strong breezes, oftentimes shedding their floral snow.  Far below, the remains of a road and bridge can be discerned beyond the deliberate cuts and angles of a long-abandoned quarry.

Obvious Exits: southeast, down, and east.

[City of Pearl, Center.]

Granting an uninhibited view of the bustling shipping industry, a stone seawall bevels out behind a long crescent bench and creates a half-moon addition to the congested crossroads at the heart of the city.  The vast water of the bay expands beyond the southern stone wall.  Ships of all sizes pass by the seafront as they make their way in and out of the harbor to the south.  The streets head in many directions, as well as a tunnel to the northeast.  At the center of the intersection is an elegantly carved monument of a giant pearl atop a tall obelisk.  The base of the centerpiece rests at the bottom of a shallow fountain that has a burning spear pointing down into the water.  A small stone sundial has been carved on the rim of the fountain. [New Archai Depository.]

A well-dressed bank teller sits comfortably behind a counter at the center of the room.  Just beyond the teller, a paneled half-wall separates the customer area from a large circular steel vault door built into the rear of the building.  You notice an open engraved silver door, and a closed large circular steel vault.

Also here: a nicely-dressed bank teller 

Obvious Exits: none

se



[Bayesian Court, Bank Entrance.]

Near the entrance of the bank, massive stone pillars create a lavish backdrop to the busy courtyard.  Interlocking stone pavers, laid out in extravagant patterns, stretch out in every direction.  Iron lamp posts and transplanted dogwood trees lie evenly spread out along the plaza with flat slabs of marble serving as benches between them.  You notice an open engraved silver door.

Also here: a white-armored sentry 

Obvious Exits: southeast, and north. 

se



[City of Pearl, Center.]

Granting an uninhibited view of the bustling shipping industry, a stone seawall bevels out behind a long crescent bench and creates a half-moon addition to the congested crossroads at the heart of the city.  The vast water of the bay expands beyond the southern stone wall.  Ships of all sizes pass by the seafront as they make their way in and out of the harbor to the south.  The streets head in many directions, as well as a tunnel to the northeast.  At the center of the intersection is an elegantly carved monument of a giant pearl atop a tall obelisk.  The base of the centerpiece rests at the bottom of a shallow fountain that has a burning spear pointing down into the water.  A small stone sundial has been carved on the rim of the fountain.  You notice a wooden directional signpost.

Also here: a navy blue-robed constable, and a white-robed constable 

Obvious Exits: southwest, southeast, northwest, northeast, west, east, and north.

help bug

Command : BUG
Usage   : BUG [YOUR BUG REPORT]
Example : bug this fountain isn't nailed down!
Short(s): 
Please use this command to submit bugs against the Shattered Isles codebase.


Some known bugs we have been experiencing:

o Adding speech quotes is bugged, resolve this by quoting only 2 or more words.
o Coinage stored within containers may not save through logging out.
o Some NPCs pick up weapons to use while already equipped with one.
o Some skills do not require stamina like they should.
o Dodge doesn't show a missed attack message, only that you've dodged one.
o Languages have not been implemented.
o Some skills may be repeatedly exploited by multiple failings.
o Some skill uses progress despite not meeting necessary material requirements, as in Firebuilding.
o While you see a # sec. delay, some or all of that delay may have happened before being displayed.
o If you are carrying more than one mining pick, it prevents mining.
o Removing resources from bundles makes the bundle worthless.
o Some commands don't work while sitting or lying.
o Trade skills continue to function after combat is initiated.
o Doors may display buggy if a shortened keyword is used, such as GO DO.  Please use a complete door word.
o When withdrawing, if the item or coin is too heavy, the clerk will drop it on the ground.
o When buying or selling, if the item or coin is too heavy, the shopkeeper will drop it on the ground.
o Some skills are still available to spirits that shouldn't be.
o On rare occasions, a room description may not display when entering a new room through a door.
o Bundling skill does not advance uses, which was intended.  It has a 100% success rate.
o Looking through an exit or open door may display incorrectly if someone is hidden in the next room.
o Arrivals channel is READ ONLY and not intended for communication.  Abusers will be turned into fish.
o Items on fire will sometimes display their (burning) tag in front of other items not on fire.
o AR/DR calculations for Bite are not displaying in the SCORE command.
o Swimming is intended to be used as a Command, not a Skill.  Due to this, all players start at level 100.
o If a player logs in while hidden, others in the room will see, "Someone returns."
o GET ALL will also try to pick up items that are nailed down, such as doors and fountains.
o Currently, there is no way to disable arrival messages, but many MUD clients can ignore or "gag" text.
o Currently, when newly deceased you may receive the messages for the commands:  Leave and Disband.
o SPLIT shares amount specified among group members, regardless of the amount of doubloons in inventory.
o Combat timer may block you from logging off for longer than it should.  Disconnect if you must go.
o When repairing, having the exact amount needed doesn't work.  Have at least 1 doubloon more than required.
o Smoking in the rain will cause your pipe to be removed back to your inventory, but it is still burning.
o Game Reboots do not currently save disguises or positions.  Flyers will fall.
o Potion values increase if sold after use.  Those caught abusing this will be burned alive.
o Foraging skills are not interrupted by non-combat abilities and spells.  This double dip is not intended.
o Cooking can continue even if one runs out of raw material, though adding new seasoning.  This is not intended.
o Movement stops foraging skills, bypassing the delay.  This is not intended.  Do not abuse it.
o Throwing food seems to cause the player to freeze.  Food Fights are suspended until further notice.
o Bundle prices are buggy if used to craft or some is removed.  Use for crafting and depositing, but sell individually.
o Pummel and blindside don't always knock out the victim as intended.
o Following death, if your AR/DR is not changing when wielding a weapon, try logging out and back in.
o Crafted items are not consistently priced.  Will require a Trade Skill overhaul to adjust.
o Sometimes on a successful Shadow Strike you are spotted by the target or another aggressive NPC before you rehide.
o Some attack spells and prayers may give uses when used against oneself, don't do it.
o Looting doesn't transfer stolen item properly at this time.
o Some items are not equipping properly due to bug in wear locations.
o Robin Hood bug in Pilfering may give away coin instead of taking it.
o Coin on skinned bodies doesn't combine with other coins, get from corpse first.
o Corpses are containers.  When left behind, items can be put inside them.

Bugs added since last update:

o Sneaking may run you out of energy to move sometimes.
o Carrying bug allows you to carry more than your maximum.

Any abuse of these or other bugs can result in severe player discipline.

A tiny trickle of water snakes along the base of a smooth, limestone crack; its patient flow creating a deep, hidden, curved pathway below ground level.  Pine boughs sway high above, their roots snaking down along the hard stone, searching out the water, and providing convenient hand holds to proceed along the otherwise smooth, wet, and slippery crevice.

[Molkreak Village, Gate.]

A large iron gate embossed with poignant lettering blocks passage any further north.  Large cliff faces on either side of the path overlook the only two ways to travel, through the gate or to the south.  Fastened to the gate is a small brass bell connected to a pulley that appears to ring when the gate is opened.  Voices, rolling carts, and the clanking sounds of nearby mechanical contraptions of which the tops are visible can be heard from within the village.  You notice a riveted copper marker, a large red painted wooden sign, a closed gnomish iron gate, and a brightly painted wooden sign.

Obvious Exits: there, and south.

s



[Narrow Crevice.]

The hard limestone surface has been polished by centuries of flowing water, leaving behind bowls, swirls, and gentle curves as it meandered along over time.  Some mosses and small tufts of grasses have taken hold, but for the most part the limestone walls remain bare and glossy.  The crevice is large enough for even the larger forest beings to move along it unseen from ground level, but the slick, irregular surfaces apparently discourage animal traffic, except for birds that swoop down from the trees in search of insects or a playful, refreshing splash-about in one of the cool, natural bowls.

Obvious Exits: west, and north. 

w



[Narrow Crevice.]

Tumbling and swirling about at the bottom of the crevice, the stream continues its relentless work slowly cutting into the hard stone.  The top of the crevice is now high above the steep, slippery limestone walls.  Evidence of the stream's past indecision lie everywhere, leaving long-forgotten ledges, slots, and pot-holes that now serve as convenient hand holds as well as natural pots for bits of grass and even the doomed sapling tree or bush.

Obvious Exits: northwest, and east. 

nw



[Narrow Crevice.]

The crevice jogs sharply from the northwest and downstream to the southeast.  The constant splash of a hip-high waterfall at the turn can be heard throughout the area.  At the waterfall's base, a basin contains a relatively calm pool.  Ice clings to the deep, dark recess just behind the falls, regardless of season.  You notice an underground cavern.
nw

Obvious Exits: southeast. 

nw



[Underground Cavern.]

The aquatic cavern is spacious due to the years of cyclic ice melt that have stripped it of all but the remaining rocky walls and crumbling stone floor.  Above, water trickles down from a shaft in the ceiling.  Areas of the uneven floor rise above the waterline, atop which lies many large bones and other uneaten remains.  The dark, flowing water that comes underneath the walls escapes through a dim crevice to the southeast.  You notice some piles of bones, a half-eaten wyvern carcass, a splintered iron-banded oak chest, a narrow crevice, a large tooth-gouged oak chest, and a large mound of ore deposits.

Obvious Exits: none
